result.final_text:
## What this letter says
An eye specialist wrote this letter to your eye doctor (optometrist). You were sent for a check of cataracts in both eyes.

- Your vision is 20/40 in the right eye. It is 20/50 in the left eye.
- Your eye pressure is 12 mmHg in both eyes.
- Your eye muscles were intact. Your side vision was full in both eyes.
- There is no relative afferent pupillary defect.
- You have a dense 3 to 4+ nuclear sclerotic cataract in each eye.
- The front of your eye (cornea) shows 1+ guttata in both eyes.
- The cup-to-disc ratio is 0.1 in both eyes.
- The vitreous, macula, vessels and edge of the eye (periphery) all look normal.

Your drop in vision seems to be caused by cataracts in both eyes.

The mild guttata in both eyes may mean early Fuchs dystrophy. This is only possible.

The specialist says you should do well with cataract surgery.

## What you need to do
1. The specialist recommended cataract surgery. You agreed to have the first eye done.
2. The letter does not list any other tasks for you.

## Dates and medicines
- Surgery on the first eye: expected "shortly". No exact date is given.
- The specialist will keep your eye doctor updated as surgery is done on each eye.
- Medicines: the letter lists none.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will my first eye surgery be?
- What does "guttata" mean for me?
- What does "possible early Fuchs dystrophy" mean for me?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
